claim: Human agents build models of their environment, which enable them to anticipate and plan upcoming events.
source: Human agents build models of their environment, which enable them to anticipate and plan upcoming events.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific consensus about human cognition.

claim: It has been proposed that hippocampal representations take the form of a predictive map-like structure, the so-called successor representation (SR).
source: Recently, it has been proposed that hippocampal representations take the form of a predictive map-like structure, the so-called successor representation (SR).
evidence: This statement references a theoretical proposal in the literature about hippocampal representations.

claim: After repeated exposure to a visual sequence A-B-C-D, presenting single sequence items (e.g., - B - -) resulted in V1 activation at the successor locations of the full sequence (e.g., C-D).
source: We found that after repeated exposure to the sequence, merely presenting single sequence items (e.g., - B - -) resulted in V1 activation at the successor locations of the full sequence (e.g., C-D), but not at the predecessor locations (e.g., A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the fMRI study described in the manuscript.

claim: After repeated exposure to a visual sequence A-B-C-D, presenting single sequence items did not result in V1 activation at the predecessor locations.
source: We found that after repeated exposure to the sequence, merely presenting single sequence items (e.g., - B - -) resulted in V1 activation at the successor locations of the full sequence (e.g., C-D), but not at the predecessor locations (e.g., A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the fMRI study described in the manuscript.

claim: Visual representations are skewed toward future states, in line with the successor representation.
source: This highlights that visual representations are skewed toward future states, in line with the SR.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings in relation to the SR model.

claim: Similar results to V1 were also found in the hippocampus.
source: Similar results were also found in the hippocampus.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from hippocampal analysis.

claim: The hippocampus developed a coactivation profile that showed sensitivity to the temporal distance in sequence space, with fading representations for sequence events in the more distant past and future.
source: Moreover, the hippocampus developed a coactivation profile that showed sensitivity to the temporal distance in sequence space, with fading representations for sequence events in the more distant past and future.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the coactivation analysis in hippocampus.

claim: V1 showed a coactivation profile that was only sensitive to spatial distance in stimulus space.
source: V1, in contrast, showed a coactivation profile that was only sensitive to spatial distance in stimulus space.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the coactivation analysis in V1.

claim: Both visual and hippocampal cortex represent a predictive map of the visual world akin to the successor representation.
source: Taken together, these results provide empirical evidence for the proposition that both visual and hippocampal cortex represent a predictive map of the visual world akin to the SR.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: The relational structure between events is learned through exposure during past experiences.
source: The relational structure, for instance that stimulus B usually follows stimulus A, is learned through exposure during past experiences (Behrens et al., 2018; Finnie et al., 2021; Gavornik and Bear, 2014) and can be used to build a model or cognitive map (Tolman, 1948) that enables us to generate inferences in situation with noisy or partial input (Ekman et al., 2017; Momennejad, 2020; Schwartenbeck et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The successor representation has been recently proposed for hippocampal representations.
source: In the context of hippocampal representations, the successor representation (SR) has been recently proposed (Dayan, 1993; Stachenfeld et al., 2017) to combine the trade-off between both flexible and efficient model properties.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: The successor representation postulates a predictive representation in which the current state is represented in terms of its future (successor) states, in a temporally discounted fashion.
source: The SR postulates a predictive representation in which the current state is represented in terms of its future (successor) states, in a temporally discounted fashion.
evidence: This is a description of the theoretical properties of the SR model.

claim: The successor representation is dependent on the actual experience, with states experienced more frequently being represented more strongly.
source: The SR is dependent on the actual experience, with states experienced more frequently being represented more strongly.
evidence: This is a description of the theoretical properties of the SR model.

claim: The successor representation enables learning in an environment without explicit reward.
source: This enables learning in an environment without explicit reward (Gläscher et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The successor representation hypothesis captures many aspects of empirical hippocampal place cell firing pattern, like the exponential decay toward distant future locations.
source: This hypothesis captures many aspects of empirical hippocampal place cell firing pattern, like the exponential decay toward distant future locations (Alvernhe et al., 2011; Mehta et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous empirical research.

claim: It remains unknown if successor representation-like representations are present outside the hippocampus in areas like the early visual cortex (V1) that have a strong retinotopic organization.
source: It remains, however, unknown if SR-like representations are present outside the hippocampus in areas like the early visual cortex (V1) that have a strong retinotopic organization.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: V1 receptive fields could theoretically become tuned to respond not only to the current input, but also to expected future inputs, analogous to hippocampal place fields.
source: Theoretically, it is possible that V1 receptive fields, analogous to hippocampal place fields, become tuned to respond not only to the current input, but also to expected future inputs.
evidence: This is a theoretical speculation about possible V1 function.

claim: The computationally efficient and flexible properties of the successor representation could in theory also underlie the anticipation of future events in V1.
source: Here, we propose that the computationally efficient and flexible properties of the SR could in theory also underlie the anticipation of future events in V1.
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal that the study aims to test.

claim: Pattern completion describes a framework in which autoassociative connections within the hippocampal CA3 regions reactivate related sequence items from partial input.
source: Pattern completion describes a framework in which autoassociative connections within the hippocampal CA3 regions reactivate related sequence items from partial input (Deuker et al., 2014; Leutgeb and Leutgeb, 2007; Rolls, 2013) that is then propagated to sensory regions such as V1 (Hindy et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Pattern completion predicts reactivations of all associated items, without any skewing toward future locations or temporal discounting of events that are farther in the future.
source: In contrast to the SR, pattern completion predicts reactivations of all associated items, without any skewing toward future locations or temporal discounting of events that are farther in the future.
evidence: This is a description of the theoretical predictions of the pattern completion model.

claim: Reactivations of future sequence locations (e.g., C-D), but not of past locations (e.g., A) were found in both V1 and hippocampus using fMRI.
source: Using fMRI, we found reactivations of future sequence locations (e.g., C-D), but not of past locations (e.g., A) in both V1 and hippocampus.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the fMRI study.

claim: A model comparison confirmed that predictive representations constitute a map-like structure, with exponential decay toward distant future states.
source: In line with the SR, a model comparison confirmed that predictive representations constitute a map-like structure, with exponential decay toward distant future states.
evidence: This claim is supported by model comparison analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Hippocampus represented visual locations based on their temporal proximity within the sequence, rather than spatial distance.
source: Further, more detailed analysis of predictive codes revealed that hippocampus represented visual locations based on their temporal proximity within the sequence, rather than spatial distance.
evidence: This claim is supported by detailed analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Humans predict upcoming visual input by using a generative model whose properties resemble the successor representation.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that humans predict upcoming visual input by using a generative model whose properties resemble the SR.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The presence of successor representation-like representations in V1 indicates that SR might be a more ubiquitous coding schema that is present beyond hippocampal place cells.
source: Importantly, the presence of SR-like representations in V1 indicates that SR might be a more ubiquitous coding schema that is present beyond hippocampal place cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Successor representation-like representations were found to be present in both V1 and hippocampus, but the predictive codes between these areas revealed complementary tuning properties.
source: Finally, while SR-like representations were found to be present in both V1 and hippocampus, the predictive codes between these areas revealed complementary tuning properties, with hippocampus being sensitive to temporal distance and V1 being more sensitive to retinotopic spatial distance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing V1 and hippocampus.

claim: Hippocampus is sensitive to temporal distance in predictive codes.
source: Finally, while SR-like representations were found to be present in both V1 and hippocampus, the predictive codes between these areas revealed complementary tuning properties, with hippocampus being sensitive to temporal distance and V1 being more sensitive to retinotopic spatial distance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from hippocampal analysis.

claim: V1 is more sensitive to retinotopic spatial distance in predictive codes.
source: Finally, while SR-like representations were found to be present in both V1 and hippocampus, the predictive codes between these areas revealed complementary tuning properties, with hippocampus being sensitive to temporal distance and V1 being more sensitive to retinotopic spatial distance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from V1 analysis.

claim: Thirty-five human observers participated in the study.
source: Human observers (N = 35) were exposed to four dots presented in rapid succession that formed an arbitrary visual sequence A-B-C-D (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental sample.

claim: Dot locations were sampled from eight locations.
source: Dot locations were sampled from eight locations (Figure 1B) and the resulting possible sequences were randomly assigned across subjects.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Participants were instructed to maintain fixation throughout the experiment.
source: Participants were instructed to maintain fixation throughout the experiment, and tasked to detect a slight temporal onset delay (170 ms vs. 17 ms) of the last sequence dot that occurred in ~40% of the full sequence trials.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: The task was designed to be demanding with a group averaged hit rate of 78% (SD = 8%).
source: The task was designed to be demanding (group averaged hit rate = 78%, SD = 8%) and to keep participants' attention on the sequence.
evidence: This is a description of the task performance data.

claim: During full sequence trials, BOLD activity at the sequence locations receiving bottom-up visual input was markedly enhanced compared to non-stimulated control locations.
source: Unsurprisingly, during full sequence trials, BOLD activity at the sequence locations receiving bottom-up visual input was markedly enhanced compared to non-stimulated control locations (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Population-based receptive field (pRF) data confirmed that the selected voxels correspond to the retinotopic stimulus locations as expected.
source: Population-based receptive field (pRF) data that was acquired for a subset of participants confirmed that the selected voxels correspond to the retinotopic stimulus locations as expected.
evidence: This claim is supported by pRF mapping data.

claim: V1 BOLD activity was enhanced at the non-stimulated successor locations compared to the non-stimulated predecessor locations during partial sequence trials.
source: In line with our predictions, V1 BOLD activity was indeed enhanced at the non-stimulated successor locations compared to the non-stimulated predecessor locations (averaged across all partial trials and sequence locations; t(34) = 6.45, p = 2.23 × 10–7).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Greater activity for successor compared to predecessor activity holds when comparing individual sequence locations without averaging.
source: Further, these results of greater activity for successor compared to predecessor activity also holds when comparing individual sequence locations without averaging (i.e., comparing non-stimulated location B when successor vs. predecessor, t(34) = 5.72, p = 2.02 × 10–6; and location C when successor vs. predecessor, t(34) = 3.13, p = 0.0035).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: A group averaged decaying factor of γ=0.14 (±0.03 s.e.m.) was found that was statistically significantly different from 1.
source: In line with our predictions, we found a group averaged decaying factor of γ=0.14 (±0.03 s.e.m.) that was statistically significantly different from 1 (non-parametric t test t(34) = –17.17, p = 2.54 × 10–18).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: No correlation between individual V1 BOLD activity and task accuracy was found in an across-subject correlation analysis.
source: However, no such correlation between individual V1 BOLD activity and task accuracy was found in an across-subject correlation analysis (see Materials and methods, spearman r = 0.05; p = 0.769).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Anticipatory activity in V1 is best described by the predictions of the successor representation compared to the co-occurrence model.
source: Our results show that anticipatory activity in V1 is best described by the predictions of the SR (Figure 4C; SR vs. CO t(34) = –2.29, p = 0.028).
evidence: This claim is supported by model comparison analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Both successor representation and co-occurrence models describe the data better than the null model.
source: Additionally, both SR and CO describe the data better than the null model (SR vs. H0 t(34) = –8.25, p = 1.24 × 10–9; CO vs. H0: t test t(34) = –7.59, p = 8.22 × 10–9).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of model comparison.

claim: Cross-validated decoding accuracies within the localizer were above chance-level in hippocampus.
source: Within localizer decoding accuracy results confirmed that hippocampus has a coarse representation of the eight stimulus locations (Figure 5B) within the localizer (two-sided one-sample t test; t(34) = 3.28, p = 0.002; cross-validated accuracy = 15 ± 3.6%, mean ± s.d.; see Materials and methods).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of decoding accuracy shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Hippocampus representations were preferentially biased toward successor locations during partial sequence trials.
source: Our results reveal that hippocampus representations were preferentially biased toward successor locations (Figure 5E; paired-sample t test, t(34) = 2.74, p = 0.009), mirroring the results found in V1.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The evidence difference time-course in hippocampus shows a transient response peaking approximately 4.7 s post-stimulus onset.
source: Results of the evidence difference time-course clearly show a transient response peaking approximately 4.7 s post-stimulus onset (Figure 5F) indicating that hippocampal predictions were triggered by the partial sequence dot.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-resolved analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: No significant relationship was observed between V1 BOLD activity and hippocampus classifier evidence in an across-subject analysis.
source: In order to probe the relationship between hippocampus and V1 successor reactivations, we performed an across-subject analysis, correlating V1 BOLD activity, averaged across all successor locations, with hippocampus classifier evidence, averaged across all successor locations. No significant relationship was observed (spearman correlation, r = –0.08, p = 0.668).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: No predictive effects were found in area V2.
source: In contrast to V1, no predictive effects were found in area V2. V2 BOLD activity was not enhanced at the non-stimulated successor locations compared to the non-stimulated predecessor locations (averaged across all partial trials and sequence locations; t(34) = 1.41, p = 0.168).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Hippocampus can contribute to a more general organization of information by representing non-spatial aspects of experience in a map-like way.
source: However, more recently, the intriguing picture emerged that hippocampus also contributes to a more general organization of information by representing non-spatial aspects of experience in a map-like way (Constantinescu et al., 2016; Garvert et al., 2017; Stachenfeld et al., 2017), similar to the representation of space (Aronov et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hippocampus representations can reflect both spatial and temporal aspects.
source: Indeed, Deuker et al., 2016 have recently shown that hippocampus representations can reflect in principle both spatial and temporal aspects.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Hippocampal representations were best described by temporal coactivation.
source: Our results show that anticipatory activity in V1 is best described by the predictions of the SR (Figure 4C; SR vs. CO t(34) = –2.29, p = 0.028).
evidence: This claim is supported by model comparison analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: V1 was best described by spatial coactivation and the absence of coactivation (H0) of sequence locations.
source: Comparing model errors (i.e., lower is better) show that hippocampal representations were best described by temporal coactivation (left), while V1 (right) was best described by spatial coactivation and the absence of coactivation (H0) of sequence locations.
evidence: This claim is supported by model comparison analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The successor representation hypothesis makes two testable predictions: that population activity represents future states over predecessor states, and that future state representations are temporally discounted.
source: The SR hypothesis makes two testable predictions, namely that population activity represents future states over predecessor states, and that future state representations are temporally discounted, such that events in the close future are more prominently represented compared to events in the distant future.
evidence: This is a description of the theoretical predictions of the SR model.

claim: V1 activity at the predecessor states showed a decrease compared to baseline.
source: Notably, this relative difference was not only due to an enhancement of successor states, but our results also showed a decrease of activity at the predecessor states (compared to baseline).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The observed decrease at the predecessor states might constitute a functional separation mechanism between predecessor and successor states.
source: We speculate that the observed decrease at the predecessor states might constitute a functional separation mechanism between predecessor and successor states, strengthening the future-directed representation of the sequence by selectively decreasing representations of the unexpected predecessor states.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The successor representation does not depend on choice-dependent reward to build its transitional task structure.
source: However, in this context, it is important to stress that the SR, unlike other model-based algorithms, does not depend on choice-dependent reward to build its transitional task structure (Momennejad et al., 2017; Stachenfeld et al., 2017) and therefore might not depend on participants' active engagement.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: Anticipatory sequence activity occurred even after subjects' attention was diverted from the sequence to a demanding task at fixation.
source: Further supporting this notion, we have previously shown that anticipatory sequence activity occurred even after subjects' attention was diverted from the sequence to a demanding task at fixation (Ekman et al., 2017), rendering the sequence task irrelevant.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: Successor representation-like representations are not limited to situations that require active planning, or multiple-choice evaluations but may rather be formed automatically and incidentally.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that SR-like representations are not limited to situations that require active planning, or multiple-choice evaluations but may rather be formed automatically and incidentally, as has been shown repeatedly in the domain of statistical learning (Fiser and Aslin, 2002; Turk-Browne et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: It is not possible to distinguish between model-based (MB) and successor representation algorithms within the context of the study design.
source: While we have interpreted the neural activity patterns in the light of the SR, it is strictly speaking not possible to distinguish between model-based (MB) and SR algorithms within the context of our design.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in the experimental design.

claim: The key distinction between successor representation and model-based algorithms is that SR caches a predictive map of states that the agent expects to visit in the future, whereas MB algorithms store a full model of the world and compute trajectories at the decision time.
source: The key distinction between them is that SR caches a predictive map of states that the agent expects to visit in the future, whereas MB algorithms store a full model of the world and compute trajectories at the decision time (Gershman, 2018; Momennejad et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: Model-based algorithms come at a higher computational cost, and are more intensive both in terms of time and working memory resources.
source: It should be noted however that MB comes at a higher computational cost, and is more intensive both in terms of time and working memory resources.
evidence: This is a description of the theoretical properties of MB algorithms.

claim: The hippocampal formation can acquire arbitrary relationships between objects beyond geometric location in space.
source: The hippocampal formation can acquire arbitrary relationships between objects (Aronov et al., 2017; Backus et al., 2016; Behrens et al., 2018; Constantinescu et al., 2016; Garvert et al., 2017) beyond geometric location in space (O'Keefe and Nadel, 1978).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hippocampus has a rudimentary representation of visual space.
source: It was recently shown that hippocampus has a rudimentary representation of visual space (Knapen, 2021; Silson et al., 2021), but it was not clear whether hippocampus would also engage in the representation of a comparably simple, low-level visual sequence presented in our paradigm.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Hippocampus representations resemble a successor representation-like predictive map, favoring future over past sequence locations.
source: Our results confirmed that hippocampus representations resemble an SR-like predictive map, favoring future over past sequence locations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Similar mechanisms might underlie spatial and non-spatial representations in hippocampus, especially if there is sequential structure present.
source: Similar to navigational space, visual space can be represented in terms of its relational structure-like direction and distance, and it has been suggested that similar mechanisms might underlie spatial and non-spatial representations (Nau et al., 2018a), especially if there is sequential structure present (Finnie et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A conceptual link between representations for visual understanding and spatial navigation has been proposed that suggests a common underlying map-like representation of visual and navigational task structure.
source: Supporting this notion, recently, a conceptual link between representations for visual understanding and spatial navigation has been proposed that suggests a common underlying map-like representation of visual and navigational task structure (Schwartenbeck et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: V1 predictions were heavily impaired after hippocampus damage.
source: Supporting the idea of functional feedback, Finnie et al., 2021 recently showed that V1 predictions were heavily impaired after hippocampus damage.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Spatiotemporal sequence predictions have been shown to occur locally within V1 without the need for top-down predictions.
source: However, contrary to this notion, spatiotemporal sequence predictions have also been shown to occur locally within V1 without the need for top-down predictions (Gavornik and Bear, 2014; Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The study showed no functional relationship between sequence prediction in V1 and hippocampus.
source: Our study showed no functional relationship between sequence prediction in V1 and hippocampus.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: V1 representations of individual sequence items resembled a coding based on spatial tuning.
source: V1 representations of individual sequence items resembled a coding based on spatial tuning.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Hippocampus represented relevant items predominantly in terms of their temporal distance within the sequence.
source: Hippocampus on the other hand represented relevant items predominantly in terms of their temporal distance within the sequence, suggesting that representations capitulate on the transitionally structure of the visual sequence.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Hippocampus can learn to represent temporal sequence structure.
source: These results align with previous reports that hippocampus can learn to represent temporal sequence structure (Thavabalasingam et al., 2018; Thavabalasingam et al., 2019) and temporal proximity in a spatial navigation task (Deuker et al., 2016; Howard et al., 2014), but to the best of our knowledge, constitute the first reports of coding temporal distance of a visual sequence.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research and claims novelty for the current findings.

claim: Hippocampus predictive codes were found to persist after the sequence task and coactivation of related sequence locations was still present during the stimulus localizer.
source: Furthermore, hippocampus predictive codes were found to persist after the sequence task and coactivation of related sequence locations was still present during the stimulus localizer, potentially indicating that hippocampus representations reflect a more stable code operating on a longer timescale.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: V1 representations did not persist throughout the stimulus localizer and reverted back to representing individual spatial locations without coactivation of related sequence locations.
source: V1 representations on the other hand did not persist throughout the stimulus localizer and reverted back to representing individual spatial locations without coactivation of related sequence locations, further highlighting another qualitative difference between V1 and hippocampus coding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The absence of successor representation-like pattern in V1 during the functional localizer is indicative of a dynamic updating of the generative model.
source: The absence of SR-like pattern in V1 during the functional localizer is therefore not at odds with our results from the main task, but rather indicative of a dynamic updating of the generative model.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: It is reasonable to speculate that predictive activity in V1 does not merely reflect top-down feedback from hippocampus, but instead that successor representation-like representations in V1 are somewhat independent, and potentially complementary, to successor representation-like representations found in the hippocampus.
source: Taken these qualitative differences together, it is reasonable to speculate that predictive activity in V1 does not merely reflect top-down feedback from hippocampus, but instead that SR-like representations in V1 are somewhat independent, and potentially complementary, to SR-like representations found in the hippocampus.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Anticipatory activity in early visual cortex and hippocampus is guided by a generative model that represents the relational structure of the visual world, akin to a predictive map.
source: In conclusion, our data show that anticipatory activity in early visual cortex and hippocampus is guided by a generative model that represents the relational structure of the visual world, akin to a predictive map.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The observed successor representation-like representation underlying visual predictions can provide a sophisticated state space representation that enables flexible generalization from partial input to future sequence locations, while also being efficient enough to provide rapid visual computations.
source: Our results suggest that the observed SR-like representation underlying visual predictions can provide a sophisticated state space representation that enables flexible generalization from partial input to future sequence locations, while also being efficient enough to provide rapid visual computations.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of the experimental findings.

claim: The experimental design, data analyses, and hypotheses were all preregistered at Open Science Framework prior to data collection.
source: The experimental design, data analyses, and hypotheses were all preregistered at Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/f8dv9/) prior to data collection.
evidence: This is a statement about the study methodology.

claim: Thirty-seven right-handed subjects participated in the fMRI study.
source: Thirty-seven right-handed subjects participated in the fMRI study.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental sample.

claim: Two participants were excluded based on predetermined performance and motion criteria during scanning.
source: Two participants were excluded based on predetermined performance and motion criteria during scanning (error rate/relative motion three standard deviations above the group mean).
evidence: This is a description of the data exclusion criteria.

claim: The final sample included 35 subjects (20 females, mean age = 27 years).
source: The final sample included 35 subjects (20 females, mean age = 27 years).
evidence: This is a description of the final experimental sample.

claim: Target sample size was decided prior to data collection based on a power analysis (two-sided paired t test, power = 80%, Cohen's d ≥ 0.5 and α = 0.05).
source: Target sample size was decided prior to data collection based on a power analysis (two-sided paired t test, power = 80%, Cohen's d ≥ 0.5 and α = 0.05).
evidence: This is a description of the sample size determination.

claim: Participants gave written informed consent in accordance with the institutional guidelines of the local ethical committee (CMO region Arnhem-Nijmegen, The Netherlands).
source: Participants gave written informed consent in accordance with the institutional guidelines of the local ethical committee (CMO region Arnhem-Nijmegen, The Netherlands) and received monetary compensation for their participation.
evidence: This is a description of the ethical approval and consent process.

claim: All participants had normal or corrected-to-normal visual acuity.
source: All participants had normal or corrected-to-normal visual acuity.
evidence: This is a description of the participant inclusion criteria.

claim: The center of each dot location was 7 degrees visual angle (dva) away from the central white fixation cross.
source: The center of each dot location was 7 degrees visual angle (dva) away from the central white fixation cross (0.5 dva) and the locations were equally spaced around the center (distance in polar angle from the vertical line: 22.5°, 67.5°, 112.5°, 157.5°, 202.5°, 247.5°, 292.5°, and 337.5°, see Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a description of the stimulus parameters.

claim: The dots had a diameter of 1.2 dva.
source: The dots had a diameter of 1.2 dva.
evidence: This is a description of the stimulus parameters.

claim: During full sequence trials, each dot was shown for 100 ms with an interstimulus interval (ISI) of 17 ms, resulting in a total sequence duration of 451 ms.
source: During full sequence trials, each dot was shown for 100 ms with an interstimulus interval (ISI) of 17 ms, resulting in a total sequence duration of 451 ms.
evidence: This is a description of the stimulus timing.

claim: For 52 out of 128 full sequence trials, the onset of the last dot was delayed with an ISI of 170 ms (instead of 17 ms).
source: For 52 out of 128 full sequence trials, the onset of the last dot was delayed with an ISI of 170 ms (instead of 17 ms).
evidence: This is a description of the task design.

claim: Participants were instructed to detect and report delayed sequence presentations via a button press with their right index finger.
source: Participants were instructed to detect and report these delayed sequence presentations via a button press with their right index finger.
evidence: This is a description of the task instructions.

claim: Sequences were constructed such that each of the eight locations served as a starting location for one possible sequence.
source: Sequences were constructed such that each of the eight locations served as a starting location for one possible sequence.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence construction.

claim: Each quadrant was stimulated once in the sequence construction.
source: Further, each quadrant was stimulated once, which also excluded the possibility that neighboring dots were part of the same sequence.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence construction constraint.

claim: The constraint that each quadrant was stimulated once was chosen to minimize the potential spreading of activity from one location to neighboring sequence locations.
source: This constraint was chosen to minimize the potential spreading of activity from one location to neighboring sequence locations.
evidence: This is a description of the rationale for the sequence construction constraint.

claim: The second dot was always presented opposite of the starting location (180° clockwise from the start).
source: Specifically, the second dot was always presented opposite of the starting location (180° clockwise from the start).
evidence: This is a description of the sequence construction rule.

claim: The third dot was shown 90° clockwise from the second location.
source: The third dot was shown 90° clockwise from the second location and the last dot was on the opposite side of the third location.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence construction rule.

claim: The last dot was on the opposite side of the third location.
source: The third dot was shown 90° clockwise from the second location and the last dot was on the opposite side of the third location.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence construction rule.

claim: These constraints served to decouple spatial and temporal distance within the sequence.
source: These constraints also served to decouple spatial and temporal distance within the sequence.
evidence: This is a description of the rationale for the sequence construction constraints.

claim: There were eight possible visual sequences that were randomly assigned and counterbalanced in frequency across subjects.
source: With these constraints, there were eight possible visual sequences that were randomly assigned and counterbalanced in frequency across subjects.
evidence: This is a description of the sequence assignment.

claim: Because within each dot sequence, temporal order and spatial distance were not perfectly decorrelated, it is not possible to estimate the combined influence of the SR model and the spatial coactivation model on the observed BOLD activity.
source: Note that because within each dot sequence, temporal order and spatial distance were not perfectly decorrelated (e.g., the second sequence dot was always farthest apart from the starting dot), it is not possible to estimate the combined influence of the SR model and the spatial coactivation model on the observed BOLD activity.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in the experimental design.

claim: The experiment lasted a total of 2 hr and consisted of three blocks: (i) learning, (ii) main task, and (iii) a stimulus localizer.

claim: During the learning part, participants were familiarized with one of the eight sequences.
source: During the learning part, participants were familiarized with one of the eight sequences.

claim: There was a delay detection task on 50% of the trials during the learning part.

claim: Participants were instructed to detect a timing delay of the last dot for which they had 1 s to respond.
source: Participants were instructed to detect a timing delay of the last dot for which they had 1 s to respond.

claim: After every 30 trials, participants were shown their aggregated detection accuracy.
source: After every 30 trials, participants were shown their aggregated detection accuracy.

claim: During the initial learning phase outside the scanner, participants received additional feedback after each trial on whether their response was correct or incorrect through changes in the color of the fixation cross.

claim: No trial-wise feedback was given inside the fMRI.
source: No trial-wise feedback was given inside the fMRI.

claim: The main task consisted of three runs of equal duration (about 13 min).
source: The main task consisted of three runs of equal duration (about 13 min).

claim: There were 192 trials per run and 576 trials in total in the main task.
source: There were 192 trials per run and 576 trials in total.

claim: Trials were separated by a variable inter-trial interval (ITI) with a duration drawn from a truncated exponential distribution with a minimum of 2 s, maximum of 10.9 s, and mean of 3.72 s.
source: Trials were separated by a variable inter-trial interval (ITI) with a duration drawn from a truncated exponential distribution with a minimum of 2 s, maximum of 10.9 s, and mean of 3.72 s.
evidence: This is a description of the trial timing.

claim: The variable ITI ensured that the experimental paradigm had no temporal structure that participants could learn to expect the onset of a trial.
source: The variable ITI ensured that the experimental paradigm had no temporal structure that participants could learn to expect the onset of a trial.
evidence: This is a description of the rationale for the variable ITI.

claim: During each run, two thirds of the 192 trials were full sequence trials (128 trials) and one third of the trials were partial sequence trials (64 trials).
source: During each run, two thirds of the 192 trials were full sequence trials (128 trials) and one third of the trials were partial sequence trials (64 trials).

claim: Trial order was pseudo-randomized with the constraint that partial sequence trials were always followed and preceded by a full sequence trial.
source: Trial order was pseudo-randomized with the constraint that partial sequence trials were always followed and preceded by a full sequence trial, excluding the possibility of partial sequence trial repetitions.

claim: There was a task on ~40% of the full sequence trials (156/384 trials).
source: There was a task on ~40% of the full sequence trials (156/384 trials).

claim: At the end of each run, participants received feedback on their performance.
source: At the end of each run, participants received feedback on their performance.
evidence: This is a description of the feedback procedure.

claim: After the main task, a functional localizer (~16 min) was run where each dot was flashed at 2 Hz for 13.5 s in a pseudo-randomized order, followed by 15 s rest period.
